body:
Continued forge-bestofboth onto other risk logic per "run it onto every logic that could benefit from it." Surveyed several other binary gates for the same defect class as WARRANT#109 (a binary decision discarding a confidence/severity signal already computed):

- WR-based min-lot ramp: already a proper smoothstep continuous curve with a "never zero" floor -- already sound, nothing to fix.
- Portfolio-heat circuit breaker + recalibration-count limiter: legitimate hard safety gates, same spirit as the SS3.6 hard floor -- correctly left as hard binary vetoes, not softened (the charter's own tested finding shows not everything benefits from continuity -- scale-out failed for exactly this reason).
- CATREC blend factor: already flagged in a prior session as needing your own judgment call before touching -- left alone.

Found one real gap: riskMgr.conservativeMode's drawdown-protection reduction applied a flat 0.7x cut the instant it triggered, discarding severity. Traced further and found the codebase ALREADY computes a continuous, loss-proportional factor for exactly this (riskMgr.parameterAdjustmentFactor, bounded 0.7-1.0, shrinks with loss severity, recovers gradually on a proven good-performance streak) -- but it was never read anywhere, a genuinely dead signal.

WARRANT#111 -> SLS(95)/10.09: replaced the flat 0.7x constant with this already-computed continuous factor. Same bounds as before (0.7 floor, 1.0 ceiling) so it can only ever be as safe as or safer than the old behavior -- just no longer blind to how severe the loss actually was. Compiled 0 errors. Deployed to the terminal's real Experts folder, ledger now at pass_92.

Two solid, evidenced warrants from this whole forge-bestofboth pass (WARRANT#109 hard floor, WARRANT#111 continuity fix), not a padded count -- reporting the survey honestly rather than manufacturing more changes from items that were already sound.
